title: Prompts in the Wild: A Large Analyzed Collection of Transactional Prompts in Code
abstract: arXiv:2608.12905v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: The behavior of contemporary generative Large Language Models (LLMs) is directly shaped by prompts, unstructured texts that describe the desired output and model behavior. In this paper we argue that prompts are linguistic objects that merit investigation in their own right. To this end, we collect 57.5K unique samples of prompts from GitHub. Specifically, we focus on transactional prompts: reproducible natural language instructions that are integrated into software. To enable the empirical, quantitative study of prompts, we introduce a structured ontology, capturing the properties of prompts as well as their formal and semantic components. Based on this ontology, we transform prompts from unstructured raw texts into richly structured linguistic objects. translated_title: 野外的提示词：代码中交易性提示词的大规模分析集合
translated_abstract: 摘要：当代生成式大语言模型（LLMs）的行为直接由提示词塑造，这些非结构化文本描述了期望的输出和模型行为。本文认为，提示词本身是值得研究的语言对象。为此，我们从GitHub收集了57.5K个独特的提示词样本。具体来说，我们专注于交易性提示词：集成到软件中的可复现自然语言指令。为了支持提示词的实证性、定量研究，我们引入了一个结构化本体论，捕捉提示词的属性及其形式和语义组成部分。基于此本体论，我们将提示词从非结构化原始文本转换为高度结构化的语言对象。对这些结构化数据的分析揭示了跨语言、领域、任务和模态的使用模式显著多样性，呈现典型的齐普夫式分布，其中一些模式明显占主导。
tldr: 本文通过收集和分析GitHub上的57.5K个交易性提示词，提出了一种结构化本体论，将提示词转化为可量化研究的语言对象，揭示了其跨领域的分布规律和使用多样性。
en_tdlr: This paper collects and analyzes 57.5K transactional prompts from GitHub, introducing a structured ontology to transform prompts into quantifiable linguistic objects, revealing Zipf-like distribution patterns and usage diversity across domains.
